facts.fact: UNICEF's chief of child protection said some of the decentralised Civil Registry sub-offices are not computerised; the document gives no date and no count, so this is dated to publication.

UNICEF and the government, through the Civil Registry Department, launched a China-funded project to computerise, digitalise and solar-power 10 decentralised Civil Registry sub-offices at 10 sites in eight districts; the launch is described only as recent, so this is dated to publication.

The computerisation of 10 Civil Registry sub-offices is funded by China and delivered by UNICEF, per UNICEF's chief of child protection; no amount is given, and the document gives no date, so this is dated to publication.

UNICEF says it is assisting the Government of Zimbabwe, through the Civil Registry Department, to computerise the 10 sub-offices, which are the department's own; dated to publication, the document giving no date.

note: The document says computerisation will let communities get digitised copies of registration documents; it does not say the sub-office will enter the birth or death digitally at registration. The 10 sub-offices are to be computerised, not yet computerised, so no offices fact is recorded.
